introduction: Identity and credentials are the gate every other Parley route sits behind: three credential kinds, a flat set of scopes, an OAuth sign-in that is the only source of an API key, and the user, key, token and organization routes the afc client already speaks to.

glossary.API key: A credential belonging to a user, issued only by the OAuth callback, acting with that user's full rights. Its string has the form af_<key_id>_<secret>.
glossary.admin token: A deployment credential with access to every workspace and user and no user identity of its own, so it can own nothing.
glossary.personal access token: A credential belonging to a user and limited to the scopes it was granted. Its string has the form af_pat_<token_id>_<secret>. Abbreviated PAT.
glossary.personal organization: The organization created for a user at first sign-in, used as the default owner of workspaces they create without naming one.
glossary.retired scope name: One of the eight scope names of earlier hub releases that a new token may no longer ask for: workspaces:create, workspaces:delete, workspaces:sync, secrets:list, secrets:manage, secrets:delete, vars:manage, vars:delete.
glossary.scope: A named permission such as workspaces:read or secrets:write. API keys and admin tokens hold every hub scope implicitly; only PATs are checked against them.

requirements.title: Authenticating a caller
requirements.rationale: Every other route in the service is gated on this one decision, so its refusals have to be exact and tell an attacker nothing.

criteria.condition: a request to a route that is not public carries no Authorization Bearer credential
criteria.action: refuse the request without running the route
criteria.contract: HTTP 401 in the error envelope with message "authentication required"; the route handler is not invoked

criteria.condition: a request carries a credential that is unknown, malformed, revoked or expired
criteria.action: refuse the request with the same answer as for no credential at all
criteria.contract: HTTP 401 in the error envelope with message "authentication required"; the message does not say which of the four conditions applied

criteria.condition: a request carries a credential the service accepts
criteria.action: identify it as an API key, a personal access token or an admin token and make that kind, and the acting user where there is one, available to the route
criteria.contract: the route sees the credential kind and, for an API key or a PAT, the user id; for an admin token it sees no user id

criteria.condition: the user behind a credential is blocked
criteria.action: refuse every request made with that credential, leaving the credential itself unrevoked
criteria.contract: HTTP 401 in the error envelope while the user is blocked; the credential's revoked_at is still null; after the user is unblocked the same credential is accepted again

criteria.action: keep every credential secret and every Authorization header out of log records and response bodies
criteria.contract: for any request carrying a credential, no log record and no response body contains the credential string or its secret portion

criteria.action: serve the public routes without a credential: the four server routes, GET /api/v1/auth/providers, POST /api/v1/auth/callback and the forge webhook ingress
criteria.contract: each public route answers its normal status to a request with no Authorization header, never 401

requirements.title: Permission scopes
requirements.rationale: A scope set that drifts from the hub's lets an existing token do more or less than its holder was promised.

criteria.action: treat an API key and an admin token as holding every hub scope, and check only personal access tokens against the scopes they were granted
criteria.contract: a route needing any hub scope admits an API key and an admin token without consulting a scope list

criteria.action: for every hub resource, treat the write scope as granting the read scope, and never treat a read scope as granting a write scope
criteria.contract: a PAT holding only <resource>:write is admitted to a route needing <resource>:read; a PAT holding only <resource>:read is refused a route needing <resource>:write

criteria.condition: a personal access token does not hold the scope a route needs
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 in the error envelope with no error_type key

criteria.condition: a token is created or amended with a retired scope name
criteria.action: refuse the request and change no token
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 in the error envelope naming the refused scope; no token is created or changed

criteria.action: register exactly the 24 hub scopes of the API reference's scope table and apikit's 8, and refuse any name outside that set
criteria.contract: a token creation naming a scope outside the registered set is 400, and each registered name is accepted

requirements.title: Signing in
requirements.rationale: OAuth is the only source of an API key, and its surprising side effect on the user's other keys is one existing automation already depends on.

criteria.condition: GET /api/v1/auth/providers is requested
criteria.action: list each configured OAuth provider with its authorize URL, without requiring a credential
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with an array of {name, authorize_url}; a Cache-Control header permitting public caching for 300 seconds

criteria.condition: POST /api/v1/auth/callback is called with a configured provider and a valid authorization code
criteria.action: create or update the user, revoke every existing API key of that user, issue one new API key, and return the user and the key together
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with body.user and body.api_key; body.api_key.key matches af_<key_id>_<secret>; every API key the user held before the call is thereafter refused 401; the new key is returned by this route and by no other

criteria.condition: POST /api/v1/auth/callback succeeds
criteria.guard: the provider identity belongs to no existing user
criteria.action: create the user and a personal organization owned by them
criteria.contract: GET /api/v1/user/orgs with the new key lists exactly one organization, owned by the new user

criteria.condition: the authorization code is invalid or expired, the redirect_uri is outside the provider's allowlist, the user is blocked, or the provider identity conflicts with an existing user
criteria.action: refuse the sign-in, creating no user and issuing no key
criteria.contract: HTTP 401 for an invalid or expired code, 400 for a disallowed redirect_uri, 403 for a blocked user and 409 for a conflicting identity; in every case no user is created or updated and no key is issued or revoked

criteria.action: accept an expires value of 0, 30, 60 or 90 days, defaulting to 90 when it is omitted, and refuse any other value
criteria.contract: the issued key's expires_at is that many days ahead, or null for 0; any other value is 400 and issues no key

requirements.title: The caller's profile
requirements.rationale: The one route afc calls to confirm a credential works.

criteria.condition: GET /api/v1/user is requested with an accepted user credential
criteria.action: return the caller's profile
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with id, username, email, full_name, status, role, provider, provider_id, created_at and updated_at

criteria.condition: PATCH /api/v1/user is called with a full_name
criteria.action: change that field and leave every other field of the user unchanged
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the updated profile; a subsequent GET returns the new full_name and the same id, username, email, role and provider

criteria.condition: PATCH /api/v1/user is called with no full_name, a null full_name or a body that is not a JSON object
criteria.action: refuse the request and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 in the error envelope; the stored profile is unchanged

requirements.title: API keys
requirements.rationale: A key that cannot be listed, rotated or revoked is a credential nobody can retire.

criteria.condition: GET /api/v1/user/keys is requested
criteria.action: list the caller's API keys as metadata only, and answer a conditional request whose ETag still matches without a body
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with an array of {key_id, created_at, expires_at, revoked_at} and an ETag header; no entry carries a secret or a hash; a repeat request carrying that ETag answers 304 with no body

criteria.condition: POST /api/v1/user/keys/:key_id/refresh is called with an API key for a key that is neither revoked nor expired
criteria.action: issue a new secret under the same key_id and recompute the expiry from the key's lifetime
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with key, key_id and expires_at; key_id is unchanged; the previous secret is thereafter refused 401 and the new one accepted

criteria.condition: the key refresh route is called with a personal access token, for a revoked or expired key, or for a key that is not the caller's
criteria.action: refuse the request and rotate nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 401 for a PAT caller, 400 for a revoked or expired key and 404 for a key that is not the caller's; the key's secret is unchanged in every case

criteria.condition: DELETE /api/v1/user/keys/:key_id is called for one of the caller's keys, including the key the request is authenticated with
criteria.action: revoke that key and complete the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 204; the request completes even when it revoked its own credential; the key is refused 401 from the next request on

criteria.condition: a key route names a key that does not exist or belongs to another user
criteria.action: answer as though the key did not exist
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 in the error envelope; the answer does not distinguish a key of another user from one that does not exist

requirements.title: Personal access tokens
requirements.rationale: PATs are how an agent gets a credential narrower than its owner's, so granting more than the grantor holds would be a privilege escalation.

criteria.condition: GET /api/v1/user/tokens is requested
criteria.action: list the caller's tokens with their permissions and no secret
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with an array of {token_id, name, permissions, expires_at, created_at, revoked_at}; no entry carries a token string or a hash

criteria.condition: POST /api/v1/user/tokens is called with a name, a non-empty permission list and a valid expires
criteria.action: create the token and return it once
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with token matching af_pat_<token_id>_<secret>; no later route returns that string; the token is accepted on a route needing one of its scopes

criteria.condition: a personal access token asks to grant a scope it does not itself hold
criteria.action: refuse the request and create or change no token
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 in the error envelope; no token is created or amended; an API key making the same request succeeds

criteria.condition: DELETE /api/v1/user/tokens/:token_id is called for a live token of the caller
criteria.action: revoke it and return its metadata
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the token's metadata and revoked_at set, not 204; the token is refused 401 from the next request on

criteria.condition: a token request has an invalid body, a missing or over-long name, an empty or malformed permission list, or an invalid expires, or names a token that is already revoked or is not the caller's
criteria.action: refuse the request and create or change no token
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 for a bad body, name, permission list or expires and for an already-revoked token; HTTP 404 for a token that is not the caller's; no token is created or changed

requirements.title: Changing a token's permissions
requirements.rationale: Three verbs over one list, one of which revokes the token, so getting the empty-list cases wrong either strands a token or deletes it by surprise.

criteria.condition: PUT, PATCH or DELETE is called on a token's permissions with a non-empty list
criteria.action: replace the token's set for PUT, add the named scopes for PATCH, and remove them for DELETE
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the token's metadata after the change; the resulting permission set is the replacement, the union, or the difference respectively; removing a scope the token does not hold leaves the set unchanged

criteria.condition: PUT is called on a token's permissions with an empty array
criteria.action: remove every permission and revoke the token
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with an empty permissions list and revoked_at set; the token is refused 401 from the next request on

criteria.condition: PATCH or DELETE is called on a token's permissions with an empty array, or any of the three is called with permissions absent or null, or for a revoked token
criteria.action: refuse the request and change no permission
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 in the error envelope; the token's permission set and revoked_at are unchanged

requirements.title: Organizations
requirements.rationale: Workspace membership is read from organizations on every request, so reading them has to work before any of that can.

criteria.condition: GET /api/v1/user/orgs is requested
criteria.action: list the organizations the caller belongs to, the personal organization among them
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with an array of {id, name, slug, url, owner_id, status, created_at, updated_at}

criteria.condition: GET /api/v1/orgs/:id is requested with an organization id
criteria.guard: the caller is a member of that organization or an admin
criteria.action: return the organization, answering a conditional request whose ETag still matches without a body
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the organization and an ETag header; a repeat request carrying that ETag answers 304 with no body

criteria.condition: GET /api/v1/orgs/:id names an organization the caller is not a member of, or one that does not exist
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 in the error envelope when the organization exists and the caller is not a member; HTTP 404 when it does not exist

requirements.title: Administration
requirements.rationale: An operator needs to create, block and retire users and organizations, and a deployment that can lose its last admin is one nobody can administer.

criteria.action: admit an administration route only to an admin token or an API key of a user holding the admin role
criteria.contract: HTTP 401 with no credential and HTTP 403 for any other accepted credential, including a PAT holding every scope

criteria.condition: an administrator creates, lists, reads, updates or deletes a user
criteria.action: apply the change and answer with the user or the list
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 on create, 200 on list, read and update, 204 on delete; a create whose username or provider identity already exists is 409; a read supports ETag and answers 304 when it matches

criteria.condition: an administrator promotes, demotes, blocks or unblocks a user
criteria.action: apply the role or status change, treating a repeat of the same change as a success
criteria.contract: HTTP 200; promoting a user who is already an admin succeeds and changes nothing; after a block the user's keys are refused and after an unblock every key that is not revoked or expired is accepted again

criteria.condition: deleting or demoting a user would leave the deployment with no active admin
criteria.action: refuse the request and leave the user's role and status unchanged
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 in the error envelope; the user is still an active admin afterwards

criteria.condition: an administrator lists or revokes another user's API keys or personal access tokens
criteria.action: answer with that user's credentials as metadata, or revoke the named one
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with entries carrying user_id and no secret; HTTP 204 on revoke, after which that credential is refused 401

criteria.condition: an administrator creates, lists, updates, deletes, blocks or unblocks an organization
criteria.action: apply the change and answer with the organization or the list
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 on create, 200 on list and update, 204 on delete; a duplicate name or slug is 409 and an invalid slug is 400

criteria.condition: an administrator lists, adds or removes an organization's members
criteria.action: answer with the membership list, or apply the addition or removal
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with memberships of {org_id, user_id, username, email, role, created_at} on list and add, 204 on remove; a user added then removed no longer appears in the list

execution_paths.title: A developer signs in and receives an API key that supersedes their old ones

steps.action: runs afc login, which requests the provider list from Parley
answers with the configured providers and their authorize URLs
authenticates the developer and returns an authorization code to afc
creates the user and a personal organization, revokes every existing API key of the user, issues a new one and returns both
sees the new key stored, and finds a previously issued key now refused 401

execution_paths.title: A scoped token is minted and refused on a route outside its scopes

steps.action: creates a personal access token granting workspaces:read alone
stores the token's hash and returns the token string once
calls a route needing tokens:manage with that token
refuses with 403 after identifying the credential and finding the scope absent
calls a route needing workspaces:read with the same token and is admitted

execution_paths.title: An administrator blocks a user and their unrevoked key stops working

steps.action: calls the block route for a user who holds a live API key
marks the user blocked without revoking any credential
makes its next request with that key and is refused 401
makes the same request again with the same key and is admitted
